# Phase 1b: Coverage planning (JGates adaptation)

Adapted from `skills/security-audit/RECONNAISSANCE.md` ("Prior-run input", "Architecture summary and companion
selection", "Deterministic coverage ledger") and `SKILL.md` ("Coverage and prior runs", "Run profiles and scope").
Upstream, the parent synthesizes `architecture.md` and seeds `coverage-ledger.json`, and `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs`
checks it. In JGates this synthesis is a fresh context that receives the validated reconnaissance facts; the host
derives every `coverage_id`, enforces the state table, seeds the prior-run units and refuses block references that do
not exist in the vendored attack-class files (the validator's role).

<!-- block:instructions -->
You are the parent's synthesis step. Using the reconnaissance facts in your brief (verify any fact you rely on by reading the source), produce the architecture summary and the coverage plan of the resolved scope. Do not hunt for findings.

Architecture summary (a hard cap of about 1,000 words): 1. product, principals, normal authority, and protected resources; 2. the comparable-software baseline, when one is source-grounded (use it to calibrate effort and severity, never to dismiss a demonstrated finding; omit it when no meaningful comparable exists); 3. tech stack, source-visible deployment paths, and offline build/test limits; 4. entry surfaces and the important source-to-sink or lifecycle paths; 5. trust boundaries and the strongest source-visible control on each; 6. workspace-relative starting paths; 7. prior coverage gaps, changed-source and blocked revalidation targets, and same-source confirmed exclusions (from the prior-run section of your brief); 8. a short companion-selection summary: selected companion files and the source-visible boundaries that require them.

Do not select a companion file merely because the language or dependency name appears. Select it because reconnaissance found the trust-sensitive boundary described by its "When to use this file" section. Do not exclude a visible boundary just because another unit reviews a related class.

Coverage plan: one unit for every material combination of entry surface, trust boundary, subsystem, and applicable ordinary or companion attack class, at the granularity of the run profile in your brief (quick: the host replaces the subsystem with the fixed all-in-scope identity; deep: split per subsystem and add a lifecycle dimension where it is material). Each dimension has a human label and a stable source-derived value in canonical_refs: a workspace-relative entry path plus exported scope, a route or message identity defined in source, the source control that defines a boundary, a package path, and the exact attack-class block reference. A block reference is FILE.md# plus the exact class name as written in bold or as a heading in that file (for companion section blocks, the heading text before any parenthetical qualifier, for example "Core discipline"). Do not derive references by lowercasing or slugging display labels. Use only the block references listed in your brief.

Seed in-scope surfaces as planned. Record a combination that does not apply as not_applicable, one outside the resolved scope as out_of_scope (never as covered), and one this source-only run cannot examine (for example a class whose decisive behavior exists only in a binary, a running service or an artifact outside the scope) as unsupported; each of these carries its reason. Every considered but unselected block goes to excluded_blocks with the source fact that excludes it. Every omission recorded by reconnaissance becomes a unit (planned when it is in scope). Record the priority rationale: unauthenticated or lowest-trust surfaces first; boundaries protecting the most valuable resources; prior-run gaps, revalidation targets and changed source before same-source re-passes; classes that historically yield confirmed findings for this target type.

Prior runs: the host has already compared the prior ledger and records in your brief with the current source. It seeds every prior unit that must return as current work (prior needs_validation, deferred, blocked, out_of_scope or changed-source units) and links carried same-source records to the current verification path; you may add units, never remove or relabel those. A prior same-source covered unit remains visible; a prior rejected record suppresses only that unchanged failed claim, not coverage of its unit. A prior quick or scoped ledger contributes only its recorded evidence and gaps, never an implied "rest is fine". If no prior ledger exists, say so in the summary.
<!-- /block -->
